drafted_from: workflow:onboard-new-buyers-in-five-days's row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json, the checklist and gap lists as workflow:set-up-a-business-on-trillion makes them, and tools/customer-follow-up/test/customer-follow-up-tools.test.mjs and tools/customer-follow-up/do-work/add-a-customer.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:onboard-new-buyers-in-five-days for the buyer sam@example.com who paid and agreed to the course emails."

lists.label: Business setup checklist
lists.holds: One row per stage of setting up the business: what is done, not done, a gap or blocked, with the status of each step.

lists.label: Business set-up gaps
lists.holds: One row per thing a stage could not close: the step, what was not decided, what this run did and the evidence.

values.undecided: No live tool sends a follow-up email after sign-up.
values.chosen: Drafted the follow-up, checked it with tool:check-copy and handed it to the person to send.
values.evidence: The workshop has no tool named send-follow-up-emails-after-sign-up.

values.undecided: The buyer did not agree to the course consent words.
values.chosen: Did not sign the buyer up.
values.evidence: consent was false for this buyer in this run.

alike: a blockers list in a project board

instructions: 1. Run workflow:set-up-a-business-on-trillion first (its write-the-business-facts and make-the-checklist steps) so record:business-setup:facts and list:business-setup-checklist exist; or pour the example rows into your own checklist (see pour).

2. Say "Run workflow:onboard-new-buyers-in-five-days". It reads the facts (read-facts), then for the buyer who paid and agreed to the consent words signs them up (sign-up-the-buyer), sends due lessons (send-due-lessons), adds them as a customer (add-the-buyer-as-a-customer) and records onboarding-day-1 (record-day-one).
3. Each later day say it again: send-due-lessons sends that day's lesson and record-day-one is repeated with the next onboarding-day step.

4. Read see-where-each-buyer-is (each customer and last step), then follow-up-after-sign-up: send-follow-up-emails-after-sign-up is not a live tool, so it is recorded as a gap and the follow-up is drafted for you to send.
5. record-the-stage ticks the onboarding row on list:business-setup-checklist and writes each gap to list:business-setup-gaps, then reads both back.

worked_examples.title: Add a paying buyer as a customer and keep the contact id
worked_examples.ask: Run workflow:onboard-new-buyers-in-five-days for the buyer Sam who paid and agreed to the course emails.
worked_examples.given: From tools/customer-follow-up/test/customer-follow-up-tools.test.mjs: tool:add-a-customer with name "Sam Example", reach_them_by "sam@example.com", came_from "buyer-after-payment", owner "Pat" keeps a customer-contact whose id starts with "contact:"; tools/customer-follow-up/do-work/add-a-customer.mjs makes that id as contact: plus a generated unique id when none is given.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
